transcript.text: Indesit dryer making a horrible squealing noise when it starts up, goes away after a few mins. Still dries fine

That squealing noise that fades after a few minutes is very typical of a drive belt losing grip on a pulley, or an idler (jockey) wheel bearing drying out. Because the dryer still works fine once it’s up to speed, the motor and drum are likely okay, but we need to check if there's friction in the drum support or belt system. Please unplug the machine first. Then try turning the drum by hand. Does it spin smoothly and quietly, or does it feel rough, gritty, or squeak as you turn it? This will tell us whether the issue is with the belt/pulley system (which often needs replacement) or something stuck inside.
Ok, unplugged it and turned the drum by hand. It turns but there's a slight squeak or scrape and it feels a little rough.

That roughness and squeak when turning by hand suggests there is a mechanical friction point in the drum support system. Since the noise disappears once running, it’s most likely that the idler (jockey) pulley bearing has dried out or worn down; as it heats up from friction, it may spin more freely for a while. The drive belt could also be glazed and slipping, but the roughness you felt points strongly to a bearing issue. To identify the correct replacement part, I need your model number—this is usually on a sticker inside the door opening or on the rear of the machine.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]

[Heading: Likely cause: jockey pulley]
Thank you for providing the model number, IDC8T3B. The symptoms—a squeal on startup that fades as it warms up, combined with a rough, scraping feel when turning the drum by hand—strongly point to a worn idler (jockey) pulley bearing. Unfortunately, I cannot confirm specific part availability or compatibility for this exact model number in my current database. Because replacing these parts requires disassembling the dryer cabinet and handling internal mechanical components, this is not a repair you can safely do yourself without specialist tools and knowledge of how your specific machine is built. I recommend contacting an appliance engineer to diagnose and replace the idler pulley (and likely the belt as well). If you wish to source parts yourself for a professional to fit, please check with a reputable spare parts supplier using your model number.
